title: Backcasting Concentrated-vs-Distributed Failure Detection: Bursty vs. Slow-Drip Sabotage

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting Concentrated-vs-Distributed Failure Detection: Bursty vs. Slow-Drip Sabotage

**Problem:** Success state: monitoring that handles both a single catastrophic action (concentrated) and many tiny harmful actions that each look benign (distributed). Backward: we need to know whether the same monitor threshold catches both, or whether distributed sabotage slips under per-action thresholds.

**Direction:** Construct synthetic agent trajectories where harm is delivered either in one obvious step or spread across many low-suspicion steps (using public APPS/SHADE-style tasks). Run an open monitor per-action and measure detection for each failure mode at matched audit budgets. Result: 'evidence that distributed sabotage evades per-action monitoring, motivating aggregate-suspicion scoring.'

**Why it matters:** UK AISI explicitly flags concentrated vs. distributed failures as needing different monitoring. Demonstrating the per-action blind spot is a crisp, lab-independent contribution on a >1yr threat model.

**Relevant context:** ai_control.md open problem on concentrated vs. distributed failures (UK AISI); 'Research Areas in AI Control' (UK AISI Alignment Project); APPS/SHADE settings are public.
